summary: Tooth #19 presents with a single-surface occlusal caries lesion covering approximately 30% of the surface with no cuspal undermining, no fracture, and no periapical pathology. The proposed D2750 porcelain crown is the most aggressive option on the restoration spectrum and is not indicated for this presentation. ADA guidelines and clinical evidence support a direct single-surface composite resin restoration (D2391) as the appropriate intervention.

decision_spectrum.label: Early smooth-surface caries (non-cavitated)
decision_spectrum.intervention: Remineralization — fluoride varnish, Arestin, hygiene protocol
decision_spectrum.reason: Lesion is cavitated and into dentin; remineralization alone is insufficient

decision_spectrum.label: Cavitated, single surface, <50% tooth structure loss
decision_spectrum.reason: MATCH: 30% occlusal lesion, no cuspal involvement, direct restoration appropriate

decision_spectrum.label: Multi-surface caries (MO, DO, MOD) or moderate structural loss
decision_spectrum.reason: Lesion is single-surface only; no interproximal component visible

decision_spectrum.label: >50% tooth structure loss, post-RCT, or fractured cusp
decision_spectrum.reason: Proposed plan — not indicated given single-surface 30% lesion without structural compromise

recommended_alternative.description: Resin-based composite — one surface, posterior, primary or permanent
recommended_alternative.rationale: Restores the carious lesion conservatively, preserves maximum tooth structure, no irreversible preparation of cusps required. Aligns with minimally invasive dentistry principles.
